display.purpose: The one headline inside the index panel. It is white, centered, capped at 19ch and uses `text-wrap: balance`.

display-skill.purpose: The skill's full name, `<project name>/<slug>`, on the compact skill panel. It is white and left-aligned, has no measure cap and breaks anywhere.

page-title.purpose: The title of a page head on Publish, Edit, Upload, Account and Add a user. It uses `text-wrap: balance` and breaks anywhere.

page-title-sm.purpose: The Page Title below 640px. The title of a page head on Publish, Edit, Upload, Account and Add a user. It uses `text-wrap: balance` and breaks anywhere.

headline.purpose: The section heading above a framed grid, such as "Skills" or "Results for …", and the compact page title on Users.

headline-sm.purpose: The Headline below 640px. The section heading above a framed grid, such as "Skills" or "Results for …", and the compact page title on Users.

doc-h1.purpose: H1 30px at -0.03em, H2 23px, H3 18px, H4 16px. The body is 400 at 15.5px and 1.7 in Body Gray. Paragraphs, lists, quotes and headings keep a 72ch measure; tables and code blocks take the full frame width. Code blocks are Red Hat Mono at 13px and 1.6, and inline code is 0.86em.

auth-title.purpose: The title inside the sign-in and setup frame, 24px above the form.

doc-h2.purpose: H1 30px at -0.03em, H2 23px, H3 18px, H4 16px. The body is 400 at 15.5px and 1.7 in Body Gray. Paragraphs, lists, quotes and headings keep a 72ch measure; tables and code blocks take the full frame width. Code blocks are Red Hat Mono at 13px and 1.6, and inline code is 0.86em.

title-lg.purpose: The title of an empty state inside a frame.

title.purpose: The full name of a skill cell, `<project name>/<slug>`, which acts as the link.

wordmark.purpose: The lowercase `skillsgist` in the nav, 8px to the right of the 24px mark. The footer uses the same form at 15px, 6px to the right of an 18px mark.

doc-h3.purpose: H1 30px at -0.03em, H2 23px, H3 18px, H4 16px. The body is 400 at 15.5px and 1.7 in Body Gray. Paragraphs, lists, quotes and headings keep a 72ch measure; tables and code blocks take the full frame width. Code blocks are Red Hat Mono at 13px and 1.6, and inline code is 0.86em.

lede.purpose: The supporting line on the panel. It is set in Ember and uses `text-wrap: pretty`. It is capped at 54ch on the index and 64ch on the skill page.

panel-title.purpose: The title in a header strip, such as Files, Versions or API token.

doc-h4.purpose: H1 30px at -0.03em, H2 23px, H3 18px, H4 16px. The body is 400 at 15.5px and 1.7 in Body Gray. Paragraphs, lists, quotes and headings keep a 72ch measure; tables and code blocks take the full frame width. Code blocks are Red Hat Mono at 13px and 1.6, and inline code is 0.86em.

page-lede.purpose: The explanation under a page title, in Body Gray, capped at 68ch, with inline Orange Ink links at the lede's own size.

doc-body.purpose: H1 30px at -0.03em, H2 23px, H3 18px, H4 16px. The body is 400 at 15.5px and 1.7 in Body Gray. Paragraphs, lists, quotes and headings keep a 72ch measure; tables and code blocks take the full frame width. Code blocks are Red Hat Mono at 13px and 1.6, and inline code is 0.86em.

body.purpose: The base size on the page, empty-state copy (52ch) and text in a field. Choice titles use it at weight 500.

body-sm.purpose: Cell descriptions, capped at 60ch and clamped to three lines.

label.purpose: Button labels, the search button and field labels. Menu items, text links, alerts, notices, the status line and table text use the same 14px at weight 400. Small buttons and the "Copy" button label drop to 13px, and the small field and row text to 13.5px.

caption.purpose: Footer text, field hints, panel meta, choice details and the sort note.

mono-command.purpose: The install command and its prompt on the orange panel.

mono-command-sm.purpose: The flat code block at every width.

mono-code.purpose: The `skillsgist login` code on the device confirmation, the one value a reader compares character by character with their terminal.

mono-code-field.purpose: The text in the code field on `/device`.

mono-figure.purpose: The count in each figure cell of a download log's source switch.

mono-editor.purpose: SKILL.md source in the full editor. The paste textarea on Publish uses the same size at 1.6.

mono-meta-lg.purpose: The values in the skill page's Details panel, the version links in the Versions list, and the versions and counts in a download log's breakdown.

mono-path.purpose: File paths in the Files list and dates and counts in tables.

mono-meta.purpose: The author handle in a cell, row sizes and timestamps, the count pill, chips, the status pill and the percentages in a download log.

mono-label.purpose: The Public, Private, admin and member labels, table column headers and the Filters label of a download log.

mono-tag.purpose: The You and Latest tags. The stacked table labels below 768px use the same size and tracking at weight 400.

mono-axis.purpose: The first and last dates under a per-day chart. The chart's peak label uses the same size with tabular numerals.

shadows.name: command-lift
shadows.purpose: Only under the raised command box on an orange panel. A tight contact shadow plus a deep ember drop.

shadows.name: popover
shadows.purpose: The open account and language menu panels and every open confirmation, the skill toolbar's Move panel included.

motion.name: ease-cf
motion.purpose: House curve for every state transition.

motion.name: duration-state
motion.purpose: Color, border and background tints on buttons, cells, figure cells, chart days, links, the search field, text fields, choice cards, the file picker, download icons and the menu chevron.

motion.name: duration-nudge
motion.purpose: The 4px rightward nudge of a hovered cell arrow.

motion.name: breathe
motion.purpose: Glow at the panel foot: opacity 0.85 to 1, scale 1 x 0.92 to 1.06 x 1.08.

motion.name: blink
motion.purpose: Orange caret block after the install command.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Stops breathe and blink and removes transitions on cells, arrows, buttons, links, figure cells, chart days and the skip link.

breakpoints.name: xs
breakpoints.purpose: Below: the skill toolbar's buttons settle into one column.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: Below: 16px gutters, one-column grid and choice cards, the sort note hidden, a 6px panel inset with 12px corners, smaller titles and figure counts, tighter form, panel and log padding, the download log's source figures in two columns, and the skill toolbar's buttons in two left-aligned columns (one column on Japanese pages). From here: the two-column grid and four source figures in a row.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: Below: tables stack into label/value rows, and the download log sets each row as a compact block with the zone on its time and a From label on its place.

breakpoints.name: column-760
breakpoints.purpose: Below: the 760px working column meets the dashed gutters, so its page head and messages take the 20px inset.

breakpoints.name: column-960
breakpoints.purpose: Below: the 960px edit column meets the dashed gutters and takes the same inset.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: Three-column grid; the skill page splits into the SKILL.md frame and a 340px aside; the skill toolbar becomes one row of divided groups with Delete at the far end; the download console sets All downloads beside the four sources and splits into a 2fr chart pane and a 1fr breakdown pane.

breakpoints.name: xl
breakpoints.purpose: Index and project panel columns widen to 1008px, command and search to 960px. Also the page max width.

components.name: Skill Toolbar
components.description: The skill page's actions in one square frame with registration marks: ghost pills with Warm Muted icons in groups split by full-height Hairline dividers, Download zip | Edit SKILL.md, Upload an archive | Make public or Make private, Move | Delete at the far end. Move and Delete are details that float a Popover panel: Move's holds a Move to project select, a hint and a small primary pill, and its pill fills Paper Shade while open; Delete's holds a hint and a danger pill naming the skill. Below 1024px the dividers drop and Delete moves under a dashed rule; below 640px the buttons settle into two columns.

narrative.overview:
skillsgist borrows the look of cloudflare.com and developers.cloudflare.com, but none of the brand. The ground is warm white paper, the text is true-gray ink, and the hairlines lean slightly toward terracotta. At the top of the index page sits one drenched orange panel with a dot-matrix texture and a slow glow at its foot. It holds the headline and the search, and says where the install commands are. The system exists to hand over one line of shell, the install command, on each project's page and each skill's page, and then get out of the way. Below the panel the registry is a square, hairline-framed grid with corner registration marks, dashed column gutters and monospace metadata. It reads more like a technical drawing than a gallery of cards. No Cloudflare logo, cloud mark or trademarked asset appears anywhere. Schibsted Grotesk and Red Hat Mono are self-hosted under the OFL as open stand-ins for Cloudflare's proprietary FT Kunst Grotesk and Apercu Mono.

The density is moderate. The panel padding is generous, body text is 15px, and each cell is at least 216px tall so a three-line description has room. Pages are server-rendered, and every interaction the system defines is native: `<details>` account and language menus and confirmations, GET and POST forms, radio cards, a Command/Prompt radio switch on the skill page and a file input. There are three exceptions. A small script copies the command block to the clipboard on one click, and without JavaScript the same click selects the whole command. A second script folds a long SKILL.md to 720px, and a long Files or Versions list to 400px, behind a Show more button, and without JavaScript everything shows. A third closes an open menu or confirmation on Escape, on a press outside it, or when focus moves out of it, and without JavaScript it stays open until its summary is pressed again. Motion is sparse and ambient. The glow at the panel foot breathes on a 7-second cycle, a caret block blinks after the command, and hover tints last 200ms. The glow, the caret and every transition switch off under reduced motion.

Every page lives in this world. The project page and the skill page keep their own orange panels, the skill page's compact and left-aligned, because they hand over an install command. The working pages (publish, edit, upload, account, users, add a user, sign-in and setup) have no orange field. They sit on the paper ground between the dashed gutters and are built from the same parts: a page head, square frames with registration marks, a Paper Shade header strip on every titled frame, 8px fields and pill buttons. Sign-in and setup center one frame on a softly masked dot field.
keyCharacteristics: At most one drenched orange panel per page, with a dot-matrix texture and a warm glow at its foot, and only on the index, a project's page and a skill's page.
A warm white paper ground, true-gray ink and terracotta-leaning hairlines.
Square, hairline-framed containers with 7px corner registration marks, and dashed column gutters that run down to the footer.
Titled frames open with a Paper Shade header strip, and forms close with a Paper Shade footer bar.
Pill-shaped buttons, 8px fields, and 12–16px corners only for the panel and the things that float.
Schibsted Grotesk at weight 500 for headings, and Red Hat Mono for commands and data.
Ember-tinted shadows, used in exactly three places: the raised command box, the open menus (account and language) and the confirmation a danger button opens.
Danger is a line and a text color, never a fill.

rules.name: The Two Oranges Rule
rules.body: Signal Orange is a field. White on it measures only 3.06:1, so the only white type it carries is the display-size panel headline; running copy on it is Ember. Anything orange that a user reads or presses uses a deeper orange instead: Action Orange behind white button labels (4.66:1), and Orange Ink for orange text on white (5.21:1) or on Peach Tint (4.92:1).

rules.name: The Ember Text Rule
rules.body: Running copy on the orange panel is set in Ember (5.52:1), never in white and never in gray. White on the panel is reserved for the display headline, the white command box, the white search button and the skill page's Command/Prompt switch.

rules.name: The One Drench Rule
rules.body: A page carries at most one full field of orange. `/`, `/p/:project` and `/p/:project/s/:slug` each carry one. On a project's page and a skill's page it sits behind that page's install command; on `/` it holds the headline and the search field, and no command. The form, account, admin, project settings and sign-in pages carry none, and an install command there sits in a flat code block on white. Everywhere else orange is a small signal: a button fill, the prompt, the caret, the focus ring, a status dot, the Public label, a checked choice, a hovered cell title, a chart bar or a share fill.

rules.name: The Warm Neutral Rule
rules.body: Grounds, hairlines and muted text lean warm, at an OKLCH hue near 50. Text inks are true neutral gray. Cool slate and blue-gray never appear in this system.

rules.name: The Quiet Danger Rule
rules.body: Danger is a line and a text color, never a fill. A danger control is set in Danger text, either as a white pill with a Danger Line border or, inside the skill toolbar, as a danger ghost, and it only gains the Danger Tint on hover. A destructive action stands apart from its neighbors: at the far end of the toolbar, or below a dashed rule. Nothing is deleted, removed or revoked on the first click: the danger button opens a confirmation that floats below it and says what happens, and only its second danger button, which names what it acts on, submits.

rules.name: The Medium Voice Rule
rules.body: Headings are set at weight 500. They get their presence from size and tight tracking, between -0.02em and -0.035em, never from bold. Weight 600 belongs only to the wordmark and to bold text inside a rendered SKILL.md.

rules.name: The Typed Data Rule
rules.body: Red Hat Mono is only for things a user would type or read as data: commands, the agent prompt a reader pastes as-is, tokens, SKILL.md source, file paths and filenames, versions, dates, sizes, author handles, counts, and the short uppercase tag, visibility, role and column labels. Sentences are never set in mono, except the agent prompt, which is pasted like a command.

rules.name: The Dashed Gutter Rule
rules.body: The edges of the content column are drawn as 1px dashed rules (5px on, 5px off, Hairline Strong). They line up with the frames' outer edges. On every page the guided section grows to fill the main column, so the gutters run from under the nav or panel down to the footer. Only square frames sit on a gutter. Wherever a column meets the gutters (always on Users, below 808px for the 760px column and below 1008px for the 960px column), everything above its first frame, the page head and any Alert, Notice or Done line, is inset 20px on both sides (18px below 640px), the compact head's inset, so the title, the message and the text inside the frames share one edge.

rules.name: The Complete Row Rule
rules.body: A framed grid never ends on a ragged row. Dot-filled cells span the leftover columns at each breakpoint: `(3 − n mod 3) mod 3` columns at the three-column width, and `n mod 2` at the two-column width.

rules.name: The Warm Shadow Rule
rules.body: Every shadow and scrim is Ember at some alpha (`rgb(60 12 0 / a)`), with a real offset and blur. Never use neutral black or a zero-offset halo.

rules.name: The Flat Frame Rule
rules.body: Frames, panels, cells, bars, forms and empty states stay flat. Lift is reserved for things that are handed over or float, and no bordered frame ever gets a shadow.

rules.name: The Square Data, Round Control Rule
rules.body: Data sits in square frames with registration marks. Anything you press to act is a pill. Anything you fill in or choose between is 8px. Only the orange panel and the surfaces floating on it or over it get 12–16px corners.

rules.name: The One-Click Copy Rule
rules.body: A command or token the user is meant to copy copies to the clipboard with one click and ends in a blinking orange caret block. Without JavaScript the same click selects it entirely, so it can still be copied by hand.

rules.name: The Header Strip Rule
rules.body: Every titled frame opens with a Paper Shade strip, at least 52px tall with a Hairline bottom border, holding its title or a filename chip on the left and its meta, count or link on the right. A form frame closes with the same Paper Shade as its footer bar, so Paper Shade marks the top and bottom of a frame and White marks its content.

dos: **Do** put white text on Signal Orange (#ff5e1f) only at display size. Set running copy and links on the orange panel in Ember (#3c0c00, 5.52:1).
**Do** fill primary buttons with Action Orange (#d63c01) and hover to #b93300. Set orange text on white in Orange Ink (#c73a02).
**Do** frame lists of records as a square hairline grid: a 1px Hairline Strong frame, 1px Hairline dividers, 7px registration marks and dot-filled cells that complete the last row.

**Do** build every other container as the same square frame with registration marks, opened by a Paper Shade header strip when it has a title, and closed by a Paper Shade footer bar when it is a form.
**Do** give text fields and selects 40px of height, 8px corners and a Hairline Strong border that turns #c9b8ae on hover and Ink on focus.

**Do** set destructive actions in #b42318 text, as danger pills (white, with a #f4c7c3 border) or, in the skill toolbar, as a danger ghost. Place them at the end of a toolbar or below a dashed rule, behind a confirmation that says what happens.
**Do** put errors in an Alert above the form, one-time information the user must act on in an orange Notice, and the confirmation of a change the page cannot show in a Done line.
**Do** use a data chip for filenames that keep their case, and an uppercase mono label only for short fixed labels.
**Do** keep Red Hat Mono for commands, tokens, SKILL.md source, paths, versions, dates, handles, counts and short uppercase labels tracked at 0.1em.
**Do** stack tables instead of scrolling them sideways: below 768px into label/value rows, and a download log below 1024px into compact rows that label only the place.
**Do** tint every shadow and scrim with Ember (`rgb(60 12 0 / a)`), with a real offset and blur.

**Do** theme the browser surfaces from the palette: Selection Peach (#ffd6c2) for selections, a 2px Signal Orange focus ring at a 2px offset (white inside the orange panel), an orange caret and accent color, and a Hairline Strong scrollbar on Paper.

**Do** limit motion to the breathing glow, the caret blink and 200–250ms state tints on `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`, and turn off the glow, the caret and anything that moves under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

**Do** build every interaction from native HTML: `<details>` for menus and confirmations, GET and POST forms, radio cards, file inputs, links and `user-select: all`. The three scripts, `public/copy.js`, `public/fold.js` and `public/dismiss.js`, only enhance: every page works without them.
**Do** draw icons as inline 16px SVG with a 1.5 stroke, round caps and joins, and `currentColor`.
**Do** self-host every face under `default-src 'self'`, as woff2 split by unicode-range with the display face preloaded.
donts: **Don't** use a Cloudflare logo, cloud mark or any trademarked Cloudflare asset. The style is borrowed, not the brand.
**Don't** take Mark Violet, Mark Rose or Mark Amber into the interface. They belong to the mark alone.
**Don't** set body text, links or button labels in white on Signal Orange (3.06:1).
**Don't** put an orange panel on a form, account, admin or sign-in page. An install command there goes in the flat code block.
**Don't** fill a button or a banner with Danger red. Danger is a line and a text color.
**Don't** bring Tailwind's slate, gray or blue utilities into any surface. Every page is on these tokens.
**Don't** turn registry items, panels or forms into rounded, shadowed cards floating on the ground. Containers are square hairline frames.
**Don't** put a shadow under a bordered frame, cell or bar.
**Don't** place a kicker or eyebrow label above a heading. A tag or chip sits beside the thing it names, or inside a header strip.
**Don't** make headings bold. Weight 500 plus tracking between -0.02em and -0.035em carries them, and tracking never goes tighter than -0.035em.
**Don't** fall back to a system face for display. If Schibsted Grotesk is not loaded, fix the font loading instead of substituting a face.
**Don't** invent counts, uptime or usage figures to fill a count pill or a headline. Show only the real length of the list.
